concept.title: What is digital audio?
concept.shortdesc: Digital audio is sound stored as numbers: samples taken thousands of times a second at a chosen precision.

conbody.p: Digital audio is sound that has been converted into a numerical representation. A few key concepts help you make better recordings and edits. If you would rather start recording, go straight to and come back later.
You do not need all of this to start recording: the default settings work well. Come back to this topic when you want to fine-tune a recording.

section.title: Waveforms
section.p: Sound travels through air as a continuous waveform of pressure changes. A microphone converts these pressure changes into an electrical signal. To store the signal digitally, the computer takes thousands of measurements, called samples, of the signal's amplitude every second.

section.title: Sample rate
section.p: The sample rate is the number of samples captured per second, measured in . Common sample rates are:

sl.sli: 44,100 Hz: CD quality, enough for most audio work
48,000 Hz: the standard for video production
96,000 Hz: used in professional music production

section.p: A higher sample rate captures more detail but produces larger files.File size grows in proportion to the sample rate: a 96 kHz file is more than twice the size of the same recording at 44.1 kHz.

section.title: Bit depth
section.p: Bit depth determines how precisely each sample's amplitude is recorded.

section.title: Key audio terms

dlentry.dd:
The height of a sound wave, corresponding to how loud the sound is. Measured in , a ratio against a reference level:
LdB = 20 log10 AA0
L (dB) = 20 log10 (A / A0)
A level of −6dB−6 dB is half the amplitude of the reference.
Distortion that occurs when the signal exceeds the maximum amplitude the system can represent. It appears as flat-topped waveforms.
Mono audio uses a single channel. Stereo uses two channels, left and right, to create a sense of width.

section.lq: Audio is measured in decibels because the ear hears ratios, not differences.
